headline: Signups prove your marketing works. Retention proves your product does.

slides.html:
Signups prove your marketing works.

Retention proves your product does.

The clearest early signal of product-market fit is not how many people arrive. It is whether some of them stay.

The chart in every board deck

Total users only goes up.

A cumulative chart counts everyone who ever signed up. It rises even when most of them left last month.

A launch, a discount or a viral post can triple signups in a week.

None of that tells you whether the product solved a problem worth coming back for.

Cohort retention

Group users by start week. Watch who keeps using it.

Cohort: everyone who started in the same week.

Retained: did the core action again in week 1, 2, 3 and so on. Not “logged in”.

Read the shape of the curve, not one number.
Two curves. Only one is a business.

Illustrative · B2B reporting tool

Signups tripled. The curve got worse.

THE LAUNCH

A big campaign brought in many new teams.

THE CURVE

New cohorts never built a first report. Retention fell to near zero.

THE FIX

Paused paid acquisition. Rebuilt onboarding around one goal: first report in ten minutes.

More users would only have filled the bucket faster.

Build the chart this week

01

Name the core action. The thing that means the product did its job.

02

Match the natural frequency. Daily for chat, weekly for planning, monthly for payroll.

03

Log it as an event with a user and a timestamp. That is all a cohort needs.

04

Review it before the roadmap. Not after the next launch.

What to remember

SHAPE OVER SIZE

A small cohort that flattens beats a big one that decays.

ORDER OF WORK

Fix retention before you buy growth.

Acquisition multiplies whatever the curve already is.

NEXT QUESTION

Who are the users who stayed?

Build for them. They are your market.

What is the core action for your product?

And does your team actually track it, or just signups?

Save this before your next growth review.
